extracted.intended_audience: ETSI members, SEP owners/declarants, implementers of ETSI standards, and other stakeholders interacting with ETSI IPR processes
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for disclosing Standard Essential Patents (SEPs) to the ETSI IPR database, the licensing undertakings expected (FRAND), data-normalisation practices, copyright and software-contribution licensing, and competition/antitrust compliance in the context of ETSI standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRAND licensing commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: ETSI’s IPR Policy is based on Fair, Reasonable And Non-Discriminatory (FRAND) licensing commitment, which balances the needs of standardisation for public use with the rights of IPR owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The basic principle of the ETSI IPR regime remains FRAND with no specific preference for any licensing model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual objectives of the IPR regime
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage IPR owners to submit their most innovative technologies with fair reward for use of their SEPs; enable implementers of ETSI standards to access such technologies under FRAND conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This double-objective underpins why ETSI requires disclosure and FRAND undertakings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to disclose SEPs to ETSI IPR database
rubrics_metrics.description: ETSI Members commit to disclose their Standard Essential Patents in the ETSI IPR database. Other stakeholders may use the same procedure to disclose their SEPs in the ETSI IPR database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the proposal or development of a standard, ETSI members must inform the Director General in a timely fashion if they are aware that they hold any patent that might be essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irrevocable undertaking to license on FRAND terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of Standard Essential Patents (SEP) holders are requested to provide an irrevocable undertaking in writing that they are prepared to grant irrevocable licenses on Fair, Reasonable And Non-Discriminatory (FRAND) terms and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This written undertaking is requested from declarants to give implementers assurance about licensing availability under FRAND.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to contact declarant before licensing/implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to making a patent licensing decision and implementing any SEP contained in the ETSI IPR Database, potential licensees shall always contact the declarant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensing terms and negotiations are commercial matters between the companies and shall not be addressed within ETSI; contacting the declarant is a procedural prerequisite before implementation/licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: ETSI neutrality on policy interpretation and licensing models
rubrics_metrics.description: ETSI does not take any position regarding the correct interpretation of its IPR policy and its IPR Guide. The ETSI IPR Policy and the IPR Guide texts stand as independent documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific licensing terms and negotiations are commercial matters between companies and shall not be addressed within ETSI. ETSI maintains no specific preference for any licensing model beyond FRAND.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to declared essential/potentially essential patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The ETSI IPR online database provides public access for information to patents which were declared as being essential or potentially essential to ETSI and 3GPP standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Potential licensees and other stakeholders may consult the database but must contact declarants before licensing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalised vs un-normalised patent number handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Normalised patent numbers are imported from the European Patent Office (EPO) Espacenet database and appear in black; un-normalised patent numbers do not match Espacenet, are created manually and appear in purple.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalised entries have direct links to EPO Espacenet for full patent information. Un-normalised numbers might be correct but are not checked and have no link to Espacenet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of bulk upload and update tools for database management
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bulk upload feature enables users to upload large amounts of SEPs in one file. The update tool enables users to update their unnormalised SEPs in reflected declarations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declarants are encouraged to update disclosures when patent-related information becomes available in the European Patent Office (EPO) database to normalise entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement to update un-normalised disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: The update tool enables users to update their unnormalised SEPs in reflected declarations; this means the patent-related information was not yet available at time of disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declarants are encouraged to update such disclosures when the data becomes available in the European Patent Office (EPO) database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright ownership of ETSI standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The ownership of the copyright in standards created by ETSI or any of its committees shall vest in ETSI. ETSI is responsible for the copyright management having all rights reserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ETSI standards are publicly available for consultation from the Standards section of the ETSI website; reproduction of parts may be allowed provided a request is made using the ETSI Copyright Licence request form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright authorisation does not imply SEP license
rubrics_metrics.description: The copyright authorisation shall never imply a license on any potential SEP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesting or receiving permission to reproduce ETSI material on copyright grounds does not grant any patent/SEP licensing rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: License terms for contributed software in standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Where software is included in any element of an ETSI standard, the software owner grants, without monetary compensation an irrevocable, non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free and sub-licensable copyright license to prepare derivative works and reproduce, display, distribute and execute the contributed software and derivative work to ETSI, ETSI members and any implementer for limited purposes (see Section 9.2 of the ETSI Directives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mandatory copyright-licensing condition for software contributions; consult Section 9.2 of the ETSI Directives for limits and details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antitrust / competition law compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Anti-trust legislation exists to prevent unfair business practices; ETSI’s position as a recognised European Standards Organisation does not exempt ETSI nor its members from the application of competition law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidelines on how to ensure compliance with relevant laws on antitrust are part of the ETSI Directives. Contact [email protected] for further information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance and user resources availability
rubrics_metrics.description: User guides and eLearning are available to assist in disclosure and database use (disclosure guide, un-normalised patents update feature guides, Power BI dashboard, CSV export files, SQL access, and an ETSI IPR Policy course).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided guides and eLearning to comply with disclosure procedures, use bulk/update features correctly, and understand policy implications.
